Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Zenpō-kōhō-fun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Zenpō-kōhō-fun|Zenpō-kōhō-fun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} {{Promising draft|reason=the high amount of work put into it over a long time, see edit history}} {{Short description|Type of Ancient Japanese Tomb}} {{Draft topics|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{AfC submission|||ts=20231110180802|u=Immanuelle|ns=118}} [[File:大安場古墳1号墳.JPG|thumb|[[Ōyasuba Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara City|ja|大田原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Chūbu Region === * {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 100 meters, {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kansai Region === * {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 183 meters, Tenri City === Chūgoku/Shikoku Region === * {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 94 meters, Matsue City * == List == * [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] *

[[File:大安場古墳1号墳.JPG|thumb|[[Ōyasuba Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara City|ja|大田原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Chūbu Region === * {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 100 meters, {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kansai Region === * {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 183 meters, Tenri City === Chūgoku/Shikoku Region === * {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 94 meters, Matsue City * == List == * [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] *

There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara City|ja|大田原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Chūbu Region === * {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 100 meters, {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kansai Region === * {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 183 meters, Tenri City === Chūgoku/Shikoku Region === * {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 94 meters, Matsue City * == List == * [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] *

{{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[ファイル:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[江戸時代]]に[[領主]]である[[徳川光圀]]の命により行われた保全整備により原型を今に伝え｢日本で一番美しい古墳｣[[森浩一]]著『古墳の発掘』[[中公新書]](65)([[中央公論社]] [[1965年]]（[[昭和]]40年）4月発行)よりといわれている[[下侍塚古墳]]]] [[ファイル:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|前方後方墳]] '''前方後方墳'''（ぜんぽうこうほうふん）は、[[古墳]]の墳形の一種であり、特に東日本の前期古墳に多く存在する。また、[[中国・四国地方]]にも多く存在し、中でも出雲地方の前方後方墳は古墳時代を通じて築かれていた。その起源は、方形の[[弥生時代の墓制#墳丘墓|墳丘墓]]への通路が変化し、突出部へと代わっていき成立したと推測されている。東日本の出現期古墳の多くは、前方後方墳であることが分かってきた。 == 概要 == 主に[[弥生時代]]後期末から前方後方墳の祖形である前方後方形墳丘墓が造られ始め[[古墳時代]]前期前半に東日本（東海・関東地方）で前方後方墳が多く造られた。100メートルを超える規模の大きな前方後方墳5基が[[大和]]に集中し、あとは下野に2基、上野・越中・美濃・駿河に1基ずつ存在する。 日本列島には約500基の前方後方墳が存在する。 === 弥生前方後方形墳丘墓 === [[愛知県]][[一宮市]]の[[西上免遺跡]]で発見された前方後方形墳丘墓は墳丘長約40メートルもある。 前方後方形墳丘墓から前方後方墳への成立に[[濃尾平野]]が重要な役割を果たしたと考えられている。3世紀前半の弥生時代終末期頃、[[東海地方]]では方形墓の周壕が一周するものや方形の一辺に突出状の祭壇を設ける墓が流行した。そしてやがてその際壇部や陸橋部が発展し前方後方形が出現する。 その例としては愛知県の[[廻間遺跡|廻間]]SZ01墳丘墓があげられ、祖形と考えられる。この墳形は西は[[京都府]]から東は[[千葉県]]までひろがった。 つまり前方後方墳は伊勢湾沿岸で誕生し各地にもたらされたと考えられる。 == 分布・規模など == ;概要 現在全国で確認されている前方後方墳は、約二百数十基である勝部昭「山代二子塚」　文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　104ページ。 現在知られている前方後方墳の規模分布を調べてみると墳丘の長さが70メートル以上は34基あり、60～70メートルは33基、50～60メートルは48基、以下規模が縮小するとともに数が増加していく。70メートルを超える前方後方墳の旧国別の築造数は、[[出雲国|出雲]]・[[美作国|美作]]・[[播磨国|播磨]]・[[摂津国|摂津]]・[[伊勢国|伊勢]]・[[尾張国|尾張]]・[[三河国|三河]]・[[能登国|能登]]・[[常陸国|常陸]]が各1基、[[美濃国|美濃]]・[[駿河国|駿河]]・[[越中国|越中]]・[[上野国|上野]]・[[出羽国|出羽]]が各2基、[[山城国|山城]]・[[陸奥国|陸奥]]が各3基、[[下野国|下野]]が4基、[[大和国|大和]]が5基であり、大規模前方後方墳も大和に集中しているといえる。さらに、100メートルを超える前方後方墳5基が大和に集中している。また、日本最長の前方後方墳は、[[天理市]]の[[西山古墳]]（180メートル、古墳時代前期）であるただし、段築の1段目だけが前方後方墳で、2段目から上は前方後円墳の型をなすという特異な型式である。同市には波多子塚古墳（144メートル、同前期）、[[下池山古墳]]（120メートル、同初期）、フサギ塚古墳（110メートル、同前〜中期）、マバカ古墳（74メートル、同最初期か）、ノムギ古墳（63メートル、同最初期か）、星塚古墳（56メートル、同後期）などが存在する。なお、墳丘最長の西山古墳は、前方後方形の基壇の上に前方後円形が乗るという非常に特異な形をしている。 ;諸学説 前方後円墳と前方後方墳の違いについて、いろいろな学説が提起されたが、まだ十分解明されていない。[[西嶋定生]]は墳形が身分秩序を示し、カバネの中でもオミを表すのが前方後方墳であるという。[[都出比呂志]]は墳形と規模から前方後方墳は[[前方後円墳体制]]という政治秩序の中では少数派的なあり方であると考えている。[[白石太一郎]]は前方後方墳を狗奴国の系譜と見る説である。東海地方に前方後方墳の起源を求める説は[[赤塚次郎]]らによって主張されてきた。 1つの説として、政治勢力としては、西日本は邪馬台国を中心とした政治連合であり、東日本は[[濃尾平野]]の狗奴国を中心として形成された政治連合であったが、東の狗奴国中心の連合は、西日本の邪馬台国連合ほど強固な連合ではなかったとするものがある。また、この濃尾平野の勢力は、[[魏志倭人伝|『魏志』倭人伝]]に記載のある[[倭]]の女王[[卑弥呼]]の[[邪馬台国]]と闘った[[狗奴国]]との関係を想定する[[学者]]もいる。 [[広瀬和雄]]は、墳丘規模がどの地域においても前方後円墳が前方後方墳を上回ること、[[東国]]においても前方後円墳と前方後方墳が併存していること、前方後円墳だけでなく前方後方墳でも最大規模のものは畿内に存在すること、副葬品に前方後円墳と前方後方墳に差がないことをあげて、畿内と東国との二項対立説を退け、前方後円墳と前方後方墳の違いは「首長層の政治的なランク付け」の反映であるとしている。広瀬和雄、「前方後円墳の世界」、p.124~128、岩波新書、2010年。 ;東海地方 [[東海地方]]の旧国名でいえば美濃・尾張・伊勢・三河などの[[濃尾平野]]を中心とする地域では、前方後方墳は36基、前方後円墳は49基確認されている。規模の上では、墳丘の長さ80メートルを超す前方後方墳は少なく、最大で[[粉糠山古墳]]（美濃）の100メートル、83メートルの北山古墳（美濃）、約80メートルの東之宮古墳（尾張）、81メートルの桜井二子古墳（三河）、71メートルの向山古墳（伊勢）などが大きな方である。ちなみにこれらの古墳の周辺には90メートル～150メートルの前方後円墳が築造されている。これらのことから古墳時代前期には、地域まで墳形と規模による身分秩序が行き渡ってはいなかったと考えられている。外表施設では、前方後円墳・前方後方墳ともに[[葺石]]が葺かれているが、[[埴輪]]は前方後方墳にはほとんどない。 [[静岡県]]の[[浜名湖]]沿岸地域の[[浜松市]]引佐町（井伊瀬谷盆地北東部の丘陵部）に4世紀後半の築造と推定される前方後方墳北岡大塚古墳（46.5メートル）が所在し、この地域の最古の古墳である。 ;中国･四国地方 中国・四国地方では、前方後円（方）墳は800基のうち前方後方墳は82基で、1割を占める。分布では、南西半分にほとんど見られず、山口県や愛媛県に認められず、九州地方にはほとんど築かれていないという傾向の延長線上にあると考えられる。北東の地域では鳥取県では希薄であり、播磨西部から岡山県北部を経て出雲地域に広がっている。出雲東部にかたよるが、山陰では因幡、伯耆に4基、石見に1基、奥に8基が存在する。 [[中国地方]]の前方後方墳は[[島根県]][[松江市]]周辺に集中して32基みられる。出雲の斐伊川中流域の三刀屋町にある松本1・2号墳が最古のものとみられている。最大は、[[岡山県]][[勝田郡]][[勝央町]]植月寺山古墳の91.5メートルである。分布では、[[山口県]]にほとんど認められなく、[[鳥取県]]・[[兵庫県]]北部地方では21基、[[広島県|広島]]・岡山両県および兵庫南部地方では48基みられる。 [[出雲]]の前方後方墳は、古墳時代を通じて築かれている点が特徴である。 [[四国地方]]では、[[徳島県]]に3基、[[愛媛県]]・[[香川県]]に1基ずつ、[[九州地方]]では、散発的に分布し、[[対馬]]をふくむ[[長崎県]]に4基、[[福岡県]]に5基みられる。 == 墳形様式 == * 前方部の平面は、矩（く）形、長方形、台形をしており、祭礼を執り行ったと考えられている。 * 後方部の平面は、方形で棺を埋葬する埋葬部を擁している。 == 各地の前方後方墳 == === 東北地方 === [[ファイル:20091231大安場古墳群1号墳.jpg|thumb|250px|[[東北地方]]最大の前方後方墳・[[大安場古墳群|大安場古墳]]]] * 京銭塚古墳（墳丘の長さ66.0メートル、[[宮城県]][[遠田郡]][[美里町 (宮城県)|美里町]]） * [[天神森古墳]]（墳丘の長さ73.5メートル、[[山形県]][[東置賜郡]][[川西町 (山形県)|川西町]]） * [[大安場古墳]]（墳丘の長さ約83メートル・東北地方最大、福島県[[郡山市]]） - 国の史跡 * [[桜井古墳]]（墳丘の長さ75.0メートル、福島県[[南相馬市]]） * [[亀ヶ森・鎮守森古墳|鎮守森古墳]]（福島県[[河沼郡]][[会津坂下町]]） - 国の史跡 * 本屋敷1古墳（墳丘の長さ36.5メートル、[[福島県]][[双葉郡]][[浪江町]]） === 関東地方 === [[File:The Mound 2,The first branch cluster,Shio Kofungun cluster of tumuli,City of Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|250px|right|塩古墳群第一支群2号墳。後方部から前方部を望む]] * {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[ファイル:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[江戸時代]]に[[領主]]である[[徳川光圀]]の命により行われた保全整備により原型を今に伝え｢日本で一番美しい古墳｣[[森浩一]]著『古墳の発掘』[[中公新書]](65)([[中央公論社]] [[1965年]]（[[昭和]]40年）4月発行)よりといわれている[[下侍塚古墳]]]] [[ファイル:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|前方後方墳]] '''前方後方墳'''（ぜんぽうこうほうふん）は、[[古墳]]の墳形の一種であり、特に東日本の前期古墳に多く存在する。また、[[中国・四国地方]]にも多く存在し、中でも出雲地方の前方後方墳は古墳時代を通じて築かれていた。その起源は、方形の[[弥生時代の墓制#墳丘墓|墳丘墓]]への通路が変化し、突出部へと代わっていき成立したと推測されている。東日本の出現期古墳の多くは、前方後方墳であることが分かってきた。 == 概要 == 主に[[弥生時代]]後期末から前方後方墳の祖形である前方後方形墳丘墓が造られ始め[[古墳時代]]前期前半に東日本（東海・関東地方）で前方後方墳が多く造られた。100メートルを超える規模の大きな前方後方墳5基が[[大和]]に集中し、あとは下野に2基、上野・越中・美濃・駿河に1基ずつ存在する。 日本列島には約500基の前方後方墳が存在する。 === 弥生前方後方形墳丘墓 === [[愛知県]][[一宮市]]の[[西上免遺跡]]で発見された前方後方形墳丘墓は墳丘長約40メートルもある。 前方後方形墳丘墓から前方後方墳への成立に[[濃尾平野]]が重要な役割を果たしたと考えられている。3世紀前半の弥生時代終末期頃、[[東海地方]]では方形墓の周壕が一周するものや方形の一辺に突出状の祭壇を設ける墓が流行した。そしてやがてその際壇部や陸橋部が発展し前方後方形が出現する。 その例としては愛知県の[[廻間遺跡|廻間]]SZ01墳丘墓があげられ、祖形と考えられる。この墳形は西は[[京都府]]から東は[[千葉県]]までひろがった。 つまり前方後方墳は伊勢湾沿岸で誕生し各地にもたらされたと考えられる。 == 分布・規模など == ;概要 現在全国で確認されている前方後方墳は、約二百数十基である勝部昭「山代二子塚」　文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　104ページ。 現在知られている前方後方墳の規模分布を調べてみると墳丘の長さが70メートル以上は34基あり、60～70メートルは33基、50～60メートルは48基、以下規模が縮小するとともに数が増加していく。70メートルを超える前方後方墳の旧国別の築造数は、[[出雲国|出雲]]・[[美作国|美作]]・[[播磨国|播磨]]・[[摂津国|摂津]]・[[伊勢国|伊勢]]・[[尾張国|尾張]]・[[三河国|三河]]・[[能登国|能登]]・[[常陸国|常陸]]が各1基、[[美濃国|美濃]]・[[駿河国|駿河]]・[[越中国|越中]]・[[上野国|上野]]・[[出羽国|出羽]]が各2基、[[山城国|山城]]・[[陸奥国|陸奥]]が各3基、[[下野国|下野]]が4基、[[大和国|大和]]が5基であり、大規模前方後方墳も大和に集中しているといえる。さらに、100メートルを超える前方後方墳5基が大和に集中している。また、日本最長の前方後方墳は、[[天理市]]の[[西山古墳]]（180メートル、古墳時代前期）であるただし、段築の1段目だけが前方後方墳で、2段目から上は前方後円墳の型をなすという特異な型式である。同市には波多子塚古墳（144メートル、同前期）、[[下池山古墳]]（120メートル、同初期）、フサギ塚古墳（110メートル、同前〜中期）、マバカ古墳（74メートル、同最初期か）、ノムギ古墳（63メートル、同最初期か）、星塚古墳（56メートル、同後期）などが存在する。なお、墳丘最長の西山古墳は、前方後方形の基壇の上に前方後円形が乗るという非常に特異な形をしている。 ;諸学説 前方後円墳と前方後方墳の違いについて、いろいろな学説が提起されたが、まだ十分解明されていない。[[西嶋定生]]は墳形が身分秩序を示し、カバネの中でもオミを表すのが前方後方墳であるという。[[都出比呂志]]は墳形と規模から前方後方墳は[[前方後円墳体制]]という政治秩序の中では少数派的なあり方であると考えている。[[白石太一郎]]は前方後方墳を狗奴国の系譜と見る説である。東海地方に前方後方墳の起源を求める説は[[赤塚次郎]]らによって主張されてきた。 1つの説として、政治勢力としては、西日本は邪馬台国を中心とした政治連合であり、東日本は[[濃尾平野]]の狗奴国を中心として形成された政治連合であったが、東の狗奴国中心の連合は、西日本の邪馬台国連合ほど強固な連合ではなかったとするものがある。また、この濃尾平野の勢力は、[[魏志倭人伝|『魏志』倭人伝]]に記載のある[[倭]]の女王[[卑弥呼]]の[[邪馬台国]]と闘った[[狗奴国]]との関係を想定する[[学者]]もいる。 [[広瀬和雄]]は、墳丘規模がどの地域においても前方後円墳が前方後方墳を上回ること、[[東国]]においても前方後円墳と前方後方墳が併存していること、前方後円墳だけでなく前方後方墳でも最大規模のものは畿内に存在すること、副葬品に前方後円墳と前方後方墳に差がないことをあげて、畿内と東国との二項対立説を退け、前方後円墳と前方後方墳の違いは「首長層の政治的なランク付け」の反映であるとしている。広瀬和雄、「前方後円墳の世界」、p.124~128、岩波新書、2010年。 ;東海地方 [[東海地方]]の旧国名でいえば美濃・尾張・伊勢・三河などの[[濃尾平野]]を中心とする地域では、前方後方墳は36基、前方後円墳は49基確認されている。規模の上では、墳丘の長さ80メートルを超す前方後方墳は少なく、最大で[[粉糠山古墳]]（美濃）の100メートル、83メートルの北山古墳（美濃）、約80メートルの東之宮古墳（尾張）、81メートルの桜井二子古墳（三河）、71メートルの向山古墳（伊勢）などが大きな方である。ちなみにこれらの古墳の周辺には90メートル～150メートルの前方後円墳が築造されている。これらのことから古墳時代前期には、地域まで墳形と規模による身分秩序が行き渡ってはいなかったと考えられている。外表施設では、前方後円墳・前方後方墳ともに[[葺石]]が葺かれているが、[[埴輪]]は前方後方墳にはほとんどない。 [[静岡県]]の[[浜名湖]]沿岸地域の[[浜松市]]引佐町（井伊瀬谷盆地北東部の丘陵部）に4世紀後半の築造と推定される前方後方墳北岡大塚古墳（46.5メートル）が所在し、この地域の最古の古墳である。 ;中国･四国地方 中国・四国地方では、前方後円（方）墳は800基のうち前方後方墳は82基で、1割を占める。分布では、南西半分にほとんど見られず、山口県や愛媛県に認められず、九州地方にはほとんど築かれていないという傾向の延長線上にあると考えられる。北東の地域では鳥取県では希薄であり、播磨西部から岡山県北部を経て出雲地域に広がっている。出雲東部にかたよるが、山陰では因幡、伯耆に4基、石見に1基、奥に8基が存在する。 [[中国地方]]の前方後方墳は[[島根県]][[松江市]]周辺に集中して32基みられる。出雲の斐伊川中流域の三刀屋町にある松本1・2号墳が最古のものとみられている。最大は、[[岡山県]][[勝田郡]][[勝央町]]植月寺山古墳の91.5メートルである。分布では、[[山口県]]にほとんど認められなく、[[鳥取県]]・[[兵庫県]]北部地方では21基、[[広島県|広島]]・岡山両県および兵庫南部地方では48基みられる。 [[出雲]]の前方後方墳は、古墳時代を通じて築かれている点が特徴である。 [[四国地方]]では、[[徳島県]]に3基、[[愛媛県]]・[[香川県]]に1基ずつ、[[九州地方]]では、散発的に分布し、[[対馬]]をふくむ[[長崎県]]に4基、[[福岡県]]に5基みられる。 == 墳形様式 == * 前方部の平面は、矩（く）形、長方形、台形をしており、祭礼を執り行ったと考えられている。 * 後方部の平面は、方形で棺を埋葬する埋葬部を擁している。 == 各地の前方後方墳 == === 東北地方 === [[ファイル:20091231大安場古墳群1号墳.jpg|thumb|250px|[[東北地方]]最大の前方後方墳・[[大安場古墳群|大安場古墳]]]] * 京銭塚古墳（墳丘の長さ66.0メートル、[[宮城県]][[遠田郡]][[美里町 (宮城県)|美里町]]） * [[天神森古墳]]（墳丘の長さ73.5メートル、[[山形県]][[東置賜郡]][[川西町 (山形県)|川西町]]） * [[大安場古墳]]（墳丘の長さ約83メートル・東北地方最大、福島県[[郡山市]]） - 国の史跡 * [[桜井古墳]]（墳丘の長さ75.0メートル、福島県[[南相馬市]]） * [[亀ヶ森・鎮守森古墳|鎮守森古墳]]（福島県[[河沼郡]][[会津坂下町]]） - 国の史跡 * 本屋敷1古墳（墳丘の長さ36.5メートル、[[福島県]][[双葉郡]][[浪江町]]） === 関東地方 === [[File:The Mound 2,The first branch cluster,Shio Kofungun cluster of tumuli,City of Kumagaya.jpg|thumb|250px|right|塩古墳群第一支群2号墳。後方部から前方部を望む]] * 勅使塚古墳（[[茨城県]]） * 丸山古墳（茨城県） * 姫塚古墳（茨城県[[東茨城郡]][[大洗町]]） * [[藤本観音山古墳]]（墳丘の長さ117.8メートル、[[栃木県]][[足利市]]） * 愛宕塚古墳（[[栃木県]]） * 大日塚古墳（栃木県） * 侍塚古墳 - 国の史跡 ** [[上侍塚古墳]]（墳丘の長さ114.0メートル、栃木県[[大田原市]]） ** (UTC)}} {{draft}} [[Category:Completion tier 7]] {{Short description|Type of Ancient Japanese Tomb}} {{Draft topics|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{AfC submission|||ts=20231110180802|u=Immanuelle|ns=118}} [[File:大安場古墳1号墳.JPG|thumb|[[Ōyasuba Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara City|ja|大田原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Chūbu Region === * {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 100 meters, {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kansai Region === * {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 183 meters, Tenri City === Chūgoku/Shikoku Region === * {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 94 meters, Matsue City * == List == * [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] *

[[File:大安場古墳1号墳.JPG|thumb|[[Ōyasuba Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara City|ja|大田原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Chūbu Region === * {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 100 meters, {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kansai Region === * {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 183 meters, Tenri City === Chūgoku/Shikoku Region === * {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 94 meters, Matsue City * == List == * [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] *

[[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara City|ja|大田原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Chūbu Region === * {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 100 meters, {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kansai Region === * {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 183 meters, Tenri City === Chūgoku/Shikoku Region === * {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 94 meters, Matsue City * == List == * [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] *

View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Zenpō-kōhō-fun|Zenpō-kōhō-fun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} {{Short description|Type of Ancient Japanese Tomb}} {{Draft topics|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{AfC submission|||ts=20231110180802|u=Immanuelle|ns=118}} [[File:大安場古墳1号墳.JPG|thumb|[[Ōyasuba Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara City|ja|大田原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Chūbu Region === * {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 100 meters, {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kansai Region === * {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 183 meters, Tenri City === Chūgoku/Shikoku Region === * {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 94 meters, Matsue City * == List == * [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] *

[[File:大安場古墳1号墳.JPG|thumb|[[Ōyasuba Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara City|ja|大田原市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Chūbu Region === * {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 100 meters, {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === Kansai Region === * {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 183 meters, Tenri City === Chūgoku/Shikoku Region === * {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – 94 meters, Matsue City * == List == * [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] *
