Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qq=}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|qq=}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishikamimen Site|qq=}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya, Aichi|qq=}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefecture|qq=}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Megaruma Site|qq=}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefecture|qq=}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri City|qq=}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishijima Sadao|qq=}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunu-koku|qq=}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konukayama Kofun|qq=}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitayama Kofun|qq=}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|qq=}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsushima Island|qq=}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daiyanba Kofun|qq=}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōriyama City|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjinmori Kofun|qq=}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|qq=}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamisamuraizuka Kofun|lt=Kamisamuraizuka Kofun|lt=Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamijisuka Kofun|qq=}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qq=}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|qq=}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishikamimen Site|qq=}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya, Aichi|qq=}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefecture|qq=}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Megaruma Site|qq=}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefecture|qq=}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri City|qq=}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishijima Sadao|qq=}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunu-koku|qq=}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konukayama Kofun|qq=}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitayama Kofun|qq=}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|qq=}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsushima Island|qq=}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' (UTC)}} {{Short description|Type of Ancient Japanese Tomb}} {{Draft topics|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{AfC submission|||ts=20231110180802|u=Immanuelle|ns=118}} [[File:大安場古墳1号墳.JPG|thumb|[[Ōyasuba Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qq=}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|qq=}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishikamimen Site|qq=}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya, Aichi|qq=}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefecture|qq=}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Megaruma Site|qq=}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefecture|qq=}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri City|qq=}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishijima Sadao|qq=}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qq=}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|qq=}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishikamimen Site|qq=}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya, Aichi|qq=}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefecture|qq=}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Megaruma Site|qq=}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefecture|qq=}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri City|qq=}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishijima Sadao|qq=}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunu-koku|qq=}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konukayama Kofun|qq=}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitayama Kofun|qq=}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|qq=}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsushima Island|qq=}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daiyanba Kofun|qq=}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōriyama City|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjinmori Kofun|qq=}} – 73.5 meters, Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]]]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|'''Zenpō-kōhō-fun'''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. {{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qq=}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|qq=}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishikamimen Site|qq=}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya, Aichi|qq=}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefecture|qq=}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Megaruma Site|qq=}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefecture|qq=}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri City|qq=}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishijima Sadao|qq=}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunu-koku|qq=}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konukayama Kofun|qq=}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitayama Kofun|qq=}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|qq=}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsushima Island|qq=}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qq=}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|qq=}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishikamimen Site|qq=}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya, Aichi|qq=}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefecture|qq=}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Megaruma Site|qq=}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefecture|qq=}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri City|qq=}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishijima Sadao|qq=}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunu-koku|qq=}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konukayama Kofun|qq=}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitayama Kofun|qq=}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|qq=}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsushima Island|qq=}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daiyanba Kofun|qq=}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōriyama City|qq=}} * {{ill|Tenjinmori Kofun|ja|天神森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjinmori Kofun|qq=}} – 73.5 meters, {{ill|Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|ja|川西町 (山形県)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawanishi Town (Yamagata Prefecture)|qq=}} === Kantō Region === * {{ill|Kamisamuraizuka Kofun|lt=Kamisamuraizuka Kofun|lt=Kamijisuka Kofun|ja|上侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamijisuka Kofun|qq=}} – 114 meters, {{ill|Ōtawara City|ja|大田原市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtawara City|qq=}} === Chūbu Region === * {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konukayama Kofun|qq=}} – 100 meters, {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mino Province|qq=}} === Kansai Region === * {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} – 183 meters, Tenri City === Chūgoku/Shikoku Region === * {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}} {{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qq=}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|qq=}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishikamimen Site|qq=}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya, Aichi|qq=}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefecture|qq=}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Megaruma Site|qq=}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefecture|qq=}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri City|qq=}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishijima Sadao|qq=}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the {{ill|Kunu-koku|ja|狗奴国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunu-koku|qq=}} lineage. ; Regional Notes * '''Eastern Japan:''' Significant examples in the Nōbi Plain include the 100-meter {{ill|Konukayama Kofun|ja|粉糠山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konukayama Kofun|qq=}} and the 83-meter {{ill|Kitayama Kofun|ja|北山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitayama Kofun|qq=}}. * '''Chūgoku Region:''' Concentrated in {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}, particularly around {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, with examples such as the {{ill|Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|ja|山代二子塚|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro Futagozuka Kofun|qq=}} (94 meters). * '''Kyūshū Region:''' Scattered distributions, including four examples on {{ill|Tsushima Island|ja|対馬市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsushima Island|qq=}}. == Kofun Features == * '''Front Sections:''' Rectangular or trapezoidal, believed to have been used for rituals. * '''Rear Sections:''' Rectangular, containing burial chambers. == Examples of Zenpō Kōhōfun == === Tōhoku Region === * {{ill|Daiyanba Kofun|ja|大安場古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daiyanba Kofun|qq=}} – 83 meters (largest in Tōhoku), {{ill|Kōriyama There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[:en:Jinyama_Kofun_Cluster|Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|{{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|1=X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}}|四隅突出形|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The {{ill|X-shaped Burial Mound|ja|四隅突出型墳丘墓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/X-shaped Burial Mound|qq=}} style is unique to the late middle Yayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]]. ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Shimosamuraizuka Kofun 2.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Edo period]] preservation and restoration directed by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qq=}}, maintaining its original form. Called "the most beautiful kofun in Japan"{{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, ''Excavation of Kofun,'' Chūō Kōron Shinsho, 1965.. Pictured: {{ill|Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimousamurai Kofun|lt=Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|ja|下侍塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimosamuraizuka Kofun|qq=}}]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zenpōkōhōfun]] '''Zenpō Kōhōfun''' (前方後方墳) is a type of [[kofun]] (ancient Kofun) in Japan. It is predominantly found among early kofun in eastern Japan, as well as in [[Chūgoku region|Chūgoku]] and [[Shikoku region|Shikoku]]. In particular, the kofun in the [[Izumo Province|Izumo]] area continued to be constructed throughout the Kofun period. This mound type is thought to have evolved from rectangular [[Yayoi period Kofuns|Yayoi Kofuns]], where pathways transformed into projections, leading to their unique shape. Many early-period kofun in eastern Japan have been identified as Zenpō Kōhōfun. == Overview == Zenpō Kōhōfun began to appear towards the end of the [[Yayoi period]], evolving from earlier rectangular Kofuns into their distinct form. Early examples were primarily constructed in eastern Japan, particularly in the [[Tōkai region]] and [[Kantō region]], during the early Kofun period. Notable examples exceeding 100 meters in length are concentrated in [[Yamato Province|Yamato]], with additional examples scattered across regions like [[Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke]], [[Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke]], and [[Mino Province|Mino]]. There are approximately 500 known Zenpō Kōhōfun across Japan. === Yayoi Zenpō Kōhō Kofuns === At the {{ill|Nishikamimen Site|ja|西上免遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishikamimen Site|qq=}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|lt=Ichinomiya City|ja|一宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya, Aichi|qq=}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aichi Prefecture|qq=}}, a Zenpō Kōhō Kofun approximately 40 meters in length was discovered. The emergence of Zenpō Kōhōfun in the [[Nōbi Plain]] is considered pivotal to their development. During the late Yayoi period (early 3rd century), tombs in the Tōkai region often featured moats surrounding rectangular Kofuns or altars extending from one side. These features eventually evolved into the characteristic projections of Zenpō Kōhōfun. Examples like the SZ01 mound at the {{ill|Megaruma Site|ja|廻間遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Megaruma Site|qq=}} in Aichi Prefecture are considered prototypes. This style spread west to {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}} and east to {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|ja|千葉県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefecture|qq=}}. == Distribution and Scale == ; General Overview Currently, approximately 200 confirmed Zenpō Kōhōfun exist nationwide.Katsube Akira, "Yamashiro Futagozuka," in ''Illustrated Japanese Historical Sites Vol. 3,'' Dōhōsha Publishing, 1991, p. 104. Of these, 34 exceed 70 meters in length, with an additional 33 measuring 60–70 meters, and 48 measuring 50–60 meters. The largest Zenpō Kōhōfun in Japan is the {{ill|Nishiyama Kofun|ja|西山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Tenri City|ja|天理市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri City|qq=}}, at 180 meters in length.The mound's first tier is Zenpō Kōhō in shape, while the second tier and above adopt a Zenpō Kōen (keyhole) shape, making it a unique hybrid. ; Scholarly Theories Various theories address the differences between Zenpō Kōenfun and Zenpō Kōhōfun. {{ill|Nishijima Sadao|ja|西嶋定生|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishijima Sadao|qq=}} argued that mound shapes reflected social hierarchy, with Zenpō Kōhōfun representing a specific Rank. {{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} considered them minority representations within the broader Zenpō Kōenfun political order. {{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}} suggested links between Zenpō Kōhōfun and the
